John Mitchell recorded a fine winning leap of 19.1/6" [?] in the Youths long-jump at the Southern Indoor Champs. at Stanmore on Jan 10th.
John Mitchell had a field day in the LCC Championships-winning the Long Jump and 100y,and coming 2nd in the 220y. This enabled the club to win the"W.J.Pepper" Trophy.

Although a foot below his best for the season, John Mitchell finished 4th in the Long jump with 22'-2¾". Martin (22.9) was unlucky to be eliminated in a 220 heat with such a good time, as was Gleeson (51.3) in the 440.

Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major. Many others who are under the guidance of Tom Carter are improving fast and the seniors will surely benefit in the very near future.
John Mitchell once again won the Long Jump,only this time smashing the meeting record by 6" with a mark of 23'2". Such was his series of jumps that he beat the second man's distance four times.

Bob's ultimate aim is the decathlon in which he could become top class,for he already has some really good field event marks behind him including a 22'6¾" long jump (achieved in the Club Champs) which ranks him as one of the top Juniors in the country behind none other than our own John Mitchell.

We also did very well on the field with good efforts by John Martin in the Shot,Discus etc.and scored maximum points in the Long Jump which has become a Belgrave parade event - thanks to Dave Ansell -John Mitchell just beating Bob Jones by ½".

Jim Vivian was an easy winner of the'A' 220 yds (23.1) whilst John Mitchell clocked a very sharp 10.3 in the 'B' 100 yds. Outstanding performance of the meeting was undoubtedly John Mitchell's exceptional 23'-2¾" long jump win.

John Mitchell became the first junior Belgrave member to ever compete for the AAA on the field,finishing 2nd in the Long Jump to P.Reed (22'9¾" [?]) with 22'3½", and Dave Rees placed 4th in the Pole Vault for London University.
In the Long Jump, John Mitchell had trouble in trying to pull out that 'big one' and was a foot below his best, nevertheless finishing 4th just behind yet another South African.

In the final, John Mitchell rocketed away from the gun and even at the first take-over the Bels had a substantial lead. With brilliant baton passing, Denis Gleeson and Chris Martin put us even further ahead and when Jim Vivian took the baton for the last leg it was all over.

Last year we won the 'W.J.Pepper' Trophy mainly due to the efforts of John Mitchell. This year John repeated his performance,improving on each of his marks, but we lost the trophy with too few other Belgravians to back him up.
John Mitchell sets his record-breaking leap of 23'-0¾" when winning the Junior long jump at the London Champs. in Sept.
Junior Club Records were set by John Mitchell (L.Jump), Jim Vivian (100y), Bob Jones (Triple Jump) and by our relay squad in both sprint relays.

There were very good performances from John Mitchell, who won the Long Jump with 22'7¾", and Bob Jones who was 3rd with 21'0"; both first year seniors and still at the height of arduous winter training schedules.
John Mitchell leaped to 22'10" in the Long Jump for 3rd place and Dave Rees, for the University team,cleared 10'4" in the Pole Vault; also 3rd.

Poly had three internationals in Campbell, Frith and Cheskin - LAC had Winbolt-Lewis and Marsh - and running in "claret and gold" were John Mitchell and Chris Martin.
In the Long Jump, John Mitchell was forced to take 2nd place behind Kelly (HHH) with Bob Couillaut 4th and Barry Townsend 6th, only 1'7" covering the first six competitors.

Derek Wade held 2nd place for most of the competition until John Mitchell, unable to produce his best form, displaced him with a 22 footer. Chris Martin started a busy couple of hours by chasing home John in the 100yds, later reversing the result in the furlong.

Good marks in the sprints and field events resulted in a pleasing win against these two strong clubs. Colin Clair and John Mitchell scored a one,two in the Shot with the former going on to grab 2nd place in the Javelin from Brian King, 3rd.

In the Long Jump, held on Saturday, John Mitchell (best of 23'2½") and Bob Jones (23'5½") were competing and we hoped that the presence of Lynn Davies, R.Stenius, etc. might inspire our duo to something really spectacular.

John Mitchell showed his superiority in the sprint, giving away 12 yds to the front markers and still winning his heat. The handicap was won with good all-round performances by John Martin, half a point ahead of Barry Townsend.

John Mitchell scored a double in the two short sprints and also placed 4th in the 440yds. Martin Hyman was Portsmouth's sole representative in the '2' and he was beaten by A.Smith for the Bels., another of the Kerr-Reilly-Barrow clan from Victoria Pk. in Scotland.
Tony Tymms of Surrey AC and our John Mitchell both clocked 9.9 in the qualifying rounds but come the final and the Surrey man just edged home first by a tenth in 9.8 .

John Mitchell is having an incredible season. Now studying medicine, he has had to cut down on his training but the heavy work of the last three years under the guidance of Dave Ansell is reaping its own reward.
We were well represented in the sprints, John Mitchell finishing extremely close to Jim Vivian in the 100y and Chris Martin grabbing 3rd in the furlong.

Four Belgravians were selected for this match, John Bicourt and Jim Vivian for the AAA and those Long Jump twins John Mitchell and Derek Wade for the University..Vivian was unlucky to be drawn outside Dick Steane in the furlong and despite finishing 2 yards down, endorsed his best of 21.9 the night…

After three rounds Peter Templeton (Bristol), the Inter-Counties winner, led with 23'0½, Alan Lerwill was close behind with 22'9½, John Mitchell was also on this mark and only scraping into the final six after two 'no-jumps, and Derek Wade in 4th spot with 22'5½.
Our only wins of the afternoon came from Peter Whewell (1m), John Mitchell (L.J) and Alan Black (3000mSC) recording a personal best of 9:15.6.

John Mitchell clocked 9.9 to qualify for the final of the '100' which was eventually won by Bob Frith (Poly) with 9.7 into a stiffish wind. John was again timed at 9.9 (the fourth time this year) for 4th place.

Derek Wade and John Mitchell both failed to reach the final eight in the Long Jump but had to contend with the toughest of opposition. Alan Lerwill did, however, compete in the final and managed to finish 7th but more significantly 3rd Briton behind Lynn Davies and Peter Reed.

Derek Wade for the second week in succession beat John Mitchell, this time with a leap of 23'1. We were invincible on the track, winning four out of the five 'B' events, placing in the first three of every other race and taking both team races (4 x 110y and 2 miles).

John Mitchell in the long jump was also highly placed with a leap in excess of 24 feet. The only other field event performance of any significance was Nick Head's winning throw in the Brockman Trophy.

Our outstanding long jumpers John Mitchell and Derek Wade must be due for higher honours next season. Many other names could be mentioned but all round we have an up and coming team which has only just begun to show its true potential.

At International level our field events section can boast of Derek Boosey in the triple jump, and John Mitchell and Alan Lerwill (2nd claim but completely Belgrave coached) in the long jump, and very close to them we have Nick Head (Javelin), Derek Wade (Long Jump), Brian King (Javelin), Frank Glass…

John Mitchell, as strong as ever, won the 'A' hundred, was second in the long jump and ran in both the relays. Chris Martin did both sprints and both of the relays.
John Mitchell had to wait until Heat 6 for his stint knowing that Piggot and Reynolds were dangerous opposition but knowing little of the South African T.
In the sprints, Jim Vivian looked more like his old self and John Mitchell powered round to an easy 220 yards win. A word of thanks to Alan Black for turning up with only 12 hours notice.

Scoring a double win in the 100 yards, Jim Vivian 9.8 and John Mitchell 10.0, Belgrave were also first in the 3000 metres steeplechase, Dick Pitrowski 9:1.4, the 'B' Mile, Bill Kerr 4.15.4 and the 'B' 220, Jim Vivian 22.2.
This was closely followed by John Mitchell with 22' 6½" in the Long Jump and later in the afternoon John Thresher won the 1500 in the excellent time of 3:44.6.

Except for John Mitchell's excellent 5th place in the Long Jump Final there was not a lot to enthuse about in Belgrave eyes at this year's Championships.
